results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

results.finding: At one year, 58% of patients randomized to anterior temporal lobectomy were free of seizures impairing awareness, against 8% of those continuing medical therapy.
results.source: Wiebe S et al., N Engl J Med 2001;345:311-318 | A randomized, controlled trial of surgery for temporal-lobe epilepsy

results.finding: In mesial temporal lobe epilepsy resistant to two drugs for no more than two years, 11 of 15 patients treated surgically and none of 23 treated medically were free of disabling seizures in the second year.
results.source: Engel J et al., JAMA 2012;307:922-930 | Early surgical therapy for drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy: a randomized trial

results.finding: Patients with disabling focal seizures of mesial temporal origin that persist despite appropriate antiseizure medication should be offered referral to an epilepsy surgery center.
results.source: Engel J et al., Neurology 2003;60:538-547 | Practice parameter: temporal lobe and localized neocortical resections for epilepsy

output.summary: Drug resistance is defined by failure of two appropriate antiseizure medication schedules. Randomized trials show that resective surgery for drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy achieves freedom from disabling seizures far more often than continued medical therapy, and guidelines recommend referral to an epilepsy surgery center.

Ictal laughter can arise from the cingulate gyrus, but MRI shows no frontal lesion and the gelastic seizures accompany a hypothalamic hamartoma.
Drop attacks from age 3 raise it, but cognition is normal and video-EEG shows focal onsets without slow spike-and-wave or generalized paroxysmal fast activity.
Stereotyped seizures since infancy with recorded electrographic onsets.

key_clinical_evidence: Gelastic seizures from infancy with treated central precocious puberty and a sessile tuber cinereum lesion on MRI are the hallmark of hypothalamic hamartoma.

Later focal impaired-awareness seizures with epigastric aura and oral automatisms, left hippocampal sclerosis on the dedicated MRI and left anterior temporal ictal onsets on video-EEG define a second, temporal epileptogenic zone (dual pathology).
Seizures persist despite valproate, levetiracetam and clonazepam: the epilepsy is drug-resistant [Kwan_2010], and surgical options for both lesions should be assessed at an epilepsy center.
Monthly focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures carry a SUDEP risk that seizure control reduces.
Long-term valproate in a young man needs counselling on possible paternal-exposure risks and contraception (MHRA and EMA 2024).

general.query: focal epilepsy in adults: definition, classification, imaging and first-line treatment

results.finding: Epilepsy is present after at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, after one unprovoked seizure with a recurrence risk of at least 60% over the next 10 years, or when an epilepsy syndrome is diagnosed.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2014;55:475-482 | ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

results.finding: Seizures are classified by onset as focal, generalized or unknown; focal seizures are described by awareness and by their first motor or non-motor feature, and may evolve to focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2017;58:522-530 | Operational classification of seizure types by the International League Against Epilepsy: position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology

results.finding: A harmonized epilepsy MRI protocol (3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at about 1 mm isotropic resolution and high-resolution coronal T2) is recommended for adults with focal epilepsy; non-dedicated protocols miss subtle lesions.
results.source: Bernasconi A et al., Epilepsia 2019;60:1054-1068 | Recommendations for the use of structural magnetic resonance imaging in the care of patients with epilepsy: a consensus report from the International League Against Epilepsy Neuroimaging Task Force

results.finding: Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is offered as first-line monotherapy for focal seizures, with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, zonisamide or lacosamide as further options.
results.source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NG217 2022 | Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

general.summary: Epilepsy is diagnosed after two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart or one with a high recurrence risk, and focal seizures are classified by onset and awareness (ILAE 2014, 2017). A dedicated epilepsy-protocol MRI is the imaging of choice (ILAE 2019). Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is first-line monotherapy for focal seizures (NICE NG217), and drug resistance is failure of two appropriate medication schedules (ILAE 2010).

additional_observations: Technique: 3T epilepsy protocol with 3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at 1 mm isotropic resolution, coronal 2 mm T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis, thin sagittal and coronal T2 through the hypothalamus, DWI and SWI. Post-contrast T1 sequences were added by the reviewing radiologist because a lesion was seen.
Comparison: outside standard MRI three years earlier: hypothalamic lesion unchanged in size; the hippocampi were not imaged with dedicated coronal sequences on that study.
No cortical malformation, heterotopia or other intracranial lesion.
Ventricular system otherwise normal in size and morphology. Normal myelination.

patient.history_present_illness: A 22-year-old right-handed male college student presents for inpatient evaluation of medically refractory epilepsy. He has a long history of seizures dating back to infancy, when his parents first noticed episodes of inappropriate, mirthless laughter lasting 10 to 20 seconds. These gelastic seizures were initially attributed to infant colic, but their stereotyped nature prompted neurological evaluation, and epilepsy was formally diagnosed at age 4. From age 3 he also had drop attacks consisting of sudden loss of postural tone, resulting in several falls with minor head injuries. At age 5, he underwent gamma knife radiosurgery targeting a lesion in the hypothalamic region, which substantially reduced the frequency of drop attacks but did not eliminate the gelastic seizures. He was also noted to have signs of early puberty at age 6, with testicular enlargement and pubic hair development, for which he received GnRH agonist therapy until age 10. Over the subsequent years, his seizure semiology evolved. In addition to the persisting gelastic episodes, he began experiencing focal seizures characterized by an epigastric rising sensation followed by loss of awareness, oral automatisms including lip smacking and swallowing, and occasional right hand fumbling. These episodes occur two to four times per week and last 30 to 90 seconds, with post-ictal confusion lasting several minutes. Approximately once per month, a focal seizure evolves to a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure. He is currently on a three-drug regimen of valproic acid, clonazepam, and levetiracetam, but seizures have remained refractory to medical therapy. He reports that the seizures significantly impair his academic performance and social life. He has never had a prolonged seizure requiring emergency intervention. He denies any recent illnesses, head trauma, sleep deprivation, or medication nonadherence. He is admitted for comprehensive epilepsy evaluation including continuous video-EEG monitoring and updated brain imaging to reassess surgical candidacy.

neurological_exam.additional: During the admission, two brief episodes of unprovoked laughter lasting 10-15 seconds were observed by nursing staff, followed by a blank stare and oral automatisms (lip smacking) lasting approximately 30 seconds. The patient had no recollection of these episodes. Post-ictally, he appeared mildly confused for 2-3 minutes before returning to baseline.
